values.en:
Terminology for set theory. The Pointer opens the complete registration module. Native declaration names and full argument indices are preserved; named `english` styles extend, rather than replace, existing upstream defaults.

| Lean constant | Style | Display template |
|---|---|---|
| `Set.Finite` | `default` | `#1 is finite` |
| `Set.Infinite` | `default` | `#1 is infinite` |
| `Set.InjOn` | `default` | `#2 is injective on #3` |
| `Set.SurjOn` | `default` | `every element of #4 is the image under #2 of an element of #3` |
| `Set.BijOn` | `default` | `#2 is a bijection from #3 onto #4` |
| `Set.MapsTo` | `default` | `#2 maps #3 into #4` |
| `Set.Pairwise` | `default` | `#2 holds for every ordered pair of distinct elements of #1` |
| `Set.range` | `default` | `\operatorname{range}(#2)` |
| `Set.prod` | `default` | `#2 \times #3` |
| `SProd.sprod` | `default` | `#4 \times #5` |
| `Set.diagonal` | `default` | `\Delta_{#0}` |
| `Set.offDiag` | `default` | `\operatorname{offDiag}(#1)` |
| `Set.EqOn` | `default` | `#2 and #3 agree on #4` |
| `Set.graphOn` | `default` | `\operatorname{graph}_{#3}(#2)` |
| `Set.LeftInvOn` | `default` | `#2 is a left inverse of #3 on #4` |
| `Set.RightInvOn` | `default` | `#2 is a right inverse of #3 on #4` |
| `Set.InvOn` | `default` | `#2 is a left inverse of #3 on #4 and a right inverse of #3 on #5` |
| `Set.Subset` | `english` | `#1 is a subset of #2` |
| `Set.Nonempty` | `english` | `#1 is nonempty` |

`SurjOn` states target coverage, not the additional `MapsTo` condition. `BijOn` includes both. Surface product notation uses `SProd.sprod`; the direct `Set.prod` declaration also has a style.

| `Set.prod` | `default` | `#2 \times #3` |
| `SProd.sprod` | `default` | `#4 \times #5` |
